---
name: Workflow Health Check Finding
about: Finding from a Skill Forge workflow run (usually auto-generated by the agent)
title: '[health-check] '
labels: 'health-check, workflow-improvement'
assignees: ''
---

## Workflow
<!-- The folder name of the workflow whose references/ folder holds the step file below, e.g. skf-create-skill
     or skf-test-skill: never a display name. -->


## Step File
<!-- The step file whose instruction bit, as its checkout path whatever install you ran: src/<workflow>/references/
     and the file's name. For a defect in a workflow's SKILL.md, a script or a shared file, the step file that was
     running. -->
`src/skf-<name>/references/<file>.md`

## Section
<!-- The slug of the heading of the section where the issue occurred: the heading without its `#`s and its numbering
     token, lower-case, one hyphen for each run of other characters than letters and digits (`### 5a. Live-Submit
     Path` gives `live-submit-path`). Never a line number. The helper command below prints it. -->


## Severity
<!-- Pick one: `bug` | `friction` | `gap`
     bug      = instructions were wrong or contradictory
     friction = instructions worked but caused back-and-forth or guessing
     gap      = a scenario arose that wasn't covered at all -->


## Fingerprint
<!-- Deterministic dedup key: first 7 hex chars of sha1("severity|workflow|step_file|section-slug|defect-key"),
     each as this issue writes it in Severity, Workflow, Step File, Section and Defect Key.
     Auto-generated by the health-check workflow and also applied as an `fp-XXXXXXX` label.
     If you are filing this manually, compute it from those five fields with SKF's helper, in a checkout: write the
     heading of the section, as the step file writes it, and the name of the thing the fix would change (see Defect
     Key) to names.json as {"section_heading": "<heading>", "defect_name": "<name>"}, and run
       uv run src/shared/scripts/skf-health-check-seen.py fingerprint --severity <severity> --workflow <workflow>
         --step-file <file>.md --stdin < names.json
     It prints the fingerprint (fp), the section fingerprint (legacy_fp), the section_slug and the defect_key.
     Write the fingerprint here alone on its line. Without push access you cannot set labels: the dedup Action reads
     this section and the Severity one, adds the labels, and links your report to any existing canonical issue.
     The section fingerprint is the same hash without the defect key: write it here only, never as a label;
     the dedup Action reads it to flag open issues that may report the same defect under another key. -->
`fp-XXXXXXX`

Section fingerprint: `fp-XXXXXXX`


## Defect Key
<!-- One to four lower-case ASCII words joined by hyphens that name the thing the fix would change, in the step
     file's or the code's own words: the most specific script (by its file name), function, script subcommand,
     field, flag or rule the fix would edit, split at underscores, dots and case changes, leading dashes, a path, an
     extension and a line suffix dropped (`floor_check` gives `floor-check`, `scripts/gate_eval.py:42` gives
     `gate-eval`). For a missing rule, name the case it should cover in two to four of the step file's words, never
     the section's subject alone. Never a line number, a severity or words from your session's story. -->


## Finding
<!-- ONE sentence. What is the problem? Do not explain why yet. -->


## Expected
<!-- ONE sentence. What did the step instruct or imply should happen? -->


## Actual
<!-- ONE sentence. What did you observe instead? -->


## Evidence
<!-- 2-5 bulleted `file:line` citations of SKF's own files: its step files, SKILL.md files, shared files and
     scripts. Quote the exact text. Never your project's code, the source a skill was built from, a brief's or a
     skill's content, or a secret: this issue is public. No narrative. -->
- `path/to/file.md:NN`: "quoted text"
-

## Impact
<!-- ONE sentence. What did this cost in this session? -->


## Suggested Fix
<!-- ONE recommended change. 1-3 sentences. Do NOT list multiple options here. -->


<details>
<summary>Alternatives considered (optional)</summary>

<!-- Only fill this if you seriously considered 2+ approaches. Keep under 100 words. -->

</details>
